objectiveScopeCuration: The DAB configuration, object and stored-procedure sources also map to security because they directly establish trusted identity context, procedure authorization and the absence of parameter-level authorization.
The permissions/secure-access training unit also maps to CI/CD because it supplies the explicit client-secret versus certificate authentication distinction used in deployment-secret design.
Source registry objective IDs, source manifest skills and question citation mappings were checked for agreement after these scoped additions.
notAdoptedFromTraining: Unconditional claims that DENY always overrides every grant, managed identity eliminates every credential risk, or isolated audit storage prevents all tampering.
Always Encrypted claims that omit the enclave trust boundary, or a four-mask taxonomy that omits the current SQL Server 2022 datetime mask.
Illustrative REST external-data-source syntax, non-URL REST credential names, resourceId casing, incomplete model-response extraction and generic Fabric AI-role assertions.
A claim that Publish always drops every target-only object, or that a successful build validates pre/post-deployment scripts and data behavior.

The reversed graphical-plan row-flow description, unconditional scan/index recommendations, universal no-blocking statements, unconditional XACT_ABORT handling, and incomplete deadlock retry snippets.
DAB GraphQL L1 caching, methods-object configuration, automatic --config merging, inferred per-parameter authorization, multiple returned procedure result sets and universal read-only view claims.
CES deployment syntax and throughput/instantaneous-delivery claims in the teaching unit; the product overview explicitly retains Preview and platform prerequisites.
Automatic complete telemetry from an environment variable alone, or a failed-request count being treated as a failure percentage.
sourceCuration.noProhibitedContent: No assessments, knowledge checks, exam dumps, copied question banks, blogs, videos, forums, internal material or unapproved GitHub implementation documents were used. No source bodies were placed outside the ignored grounding area.

duplicatesAndQuality.limitations: Deterministic checks do not establish semantic originality or reviewer independence. All archive concept/stem descriptions were inspected during authoring; independent reviewers must still challenge duplicates within the integrated full bank and across credentials.
relatedConceptDistinctions: The new DAB cache item addresses REST-only applicability, not archived global/entity opt-in, entity TTL fallback or configuration-file relationships.
The new CDC item addresses replication's shared log-reader dependency, not archived capture latency, update operation codes, retention-window gaps or capture-instance column transitions.
The role-delegation question requires AS role for onward delegation; it is not the archived removal of a grant option or ordinary schema/table grant scope.
The audit additions address Entra pre-database failures and independent archive access, not archived disabled audit objects, orphaned audit GUIDs or audit-file read permissions.
The new SNAPSHOT write-conflict item differs from the preserved read-consistency choice and deadlock-victim recovery by requiring a fresh read and business recalculation.

authorWarningNotes.dp800-direct-013: Negative/absolute heuristics concern the necessary no-enclave and engine-boundary constraints. The original wording is retained; its deep explanation explicitly limits equality-pattern secrecy.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-direct-017: The pronoun refers to the proposed source-to-target deployment, whose requested T-SQL artifact is explicitly named.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-direct-020: The configuration and installed-version references refer to the same DAB stored-procedure endpoint; the omitted-method and no-overlay conditions are explicit.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-001: The prerequisite wording concerns the specific closed symmetric key. Named source/destination types and usable certificate prevent treating the requirement as a universal encryption statement.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-003: The negative constraint protects the sensitive lookup from direct SELECT; the policy, predicate function and business table have distinct explicit roles.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-004: Mira, ProcedureDelegates and NewReader have separately stated roles in the permission chain; pronouns do not select an unstated grantor.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-008: The missing audit events are explicitly rejected before database access; the explanation does not generalize that cause to every missing audit event.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-009: The no-service-write requirement applies to archived copies, not active files. Both locations and their principals are named to preserve that distinction.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-010: Only-system-assigned authorization is a stipulated incident condition, not a general assertion about supported identities.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-011: The restriction against whole-resource credential scope is a required least-privilege boundary. The exact arc/archive segments make the distinction observable.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-012: The trusted context is distinguished from request TenantId and shared SQL execution identity; authorization is not inferred from a path name or POST body.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-013: Read-only prompt wording is intentionally contrasted with enforced authority. The answer does not claim a complete prompt-injection defense or a universal MCP configuration schema.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-014: The single-database storage requirement is a finite capacity constraint, not an unlimited-growth or performance guarantee. The question is Intermediate.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-015: The exclusions separate plan-cache storage from parallelism and regression repair; the task remains a positive setting-selection question.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-016: The first and concurrent transactions are distinguished by their reads and commits. The safe-retry condition does not promise arbitrary business operations are idempotent.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-017: Historical and current evidence refer to the same query, but to different stores and execution contexts; both required evidence dimensions are stated.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-018: Session 52 is explicitly identified as the sleeping lock owner; downstream session numbers and wait direction avoid an ambiguous head-blocker pronoun.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-019: The incorrect amount and cross-object state risks are explicit. Each requested test targets one defect rather than asking the reader to infer missing acceptance criteria.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-020: The no-weakened-results condition preserves meaningful assertions. Data contamination and a dedicated test target are explicit.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-021: The exclusion from model compilation is not deletion from the repository or deployment package; the three file responsibilities are deliberately separated.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-022: The older-version exclusion states a hypothetical documented feature boundary. No unnamed feature's detailed syntax or maturity is invented.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-023: The CLR-containing project and built artifact are separate referents; the answer preserves that stage distinction.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-024: The .dacpac is clearly a generated release artifact, not the source files to be reviewed. The item is intentionally foundational.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-026: Both accepted intentions are explicit. A compiling alternative that retains the rejected legacy column would abandon one of them.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-027: The absent business decision is intentional and does not invent one. The positive task is resolving a conflicting PR contract before approval.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-028: Authorized-job-only retrieval is a security requirement, not a claim that a vault prevents every leak; the explanation explicitly retains access and logging responsibilities.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-030: The approved hotfix and unrelated monitoring object are distinct. The chosen source/target direction is tied to importing into the project.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-032: The prerequisite rename and already-calculated plan are explicit. The response asks for controlled staged validation rather than an automatic live repair.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-033: The existing pipeline and resulting artifact are named. Pre-merge validation and pre-production approval remain separate referents and controls.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-035: The pinned runtime and latest schema are distinct version references. Changing editor metadata is not portrayed as an executable upgrade.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-037: The returned endCursor is the continuation value; exposed field names and physical column names are explicitly distinguished.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-039: The inability to infer a view key is documented. The explicit stable unique RegionCode premise avoids assuming an arbitrary view column is a key.
authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-040: The source customer, target invoices and join columns are explicitly named. The straightforward mapping is Intermediate, not inflated to Advanced.

authorWarningNotes.dp800-20260916-d2-045: The capture-job statement is conditioned on an existing transactional publication. It does not claim every CDC configuration uses the replication reader.
